tip: "ou" [u] is the Arabic long و (as in نور). "u" [y] has no Arabic equivalent: say ي (ee), keep your tongue there, then round your lips as for و.
Same ou/u contrast. Bonus: the French r is very close to Arabic غ, so use it!
Lips are rounded for both, only the tongue moves: ou = tongue pulled back (و); u = tongue forward as for ي.
Not a true minimal pair: listen for the extra syllable "-coup" [ku]. "beau" ends on a tight, closed o with no English "bow" glide. Stress the LAST syllable: beau-COUP.
é [e]: smile, tongue high, short and tense, with no English "ay" glide. ai/è [ɛ]: open the mouth a little more, like the "e" in "bed". Standard French keeps them apart.
Nasal vowels: never pronounce the n. in/ain [ɛ̃]: lips spread, like the "a" in "bad" sent through the nose. an/en [ɑ̃]: mouth wide open, "ah" through the nose.
an/en [ɑ̃]: open "ah" through the nose, lips relaxed. on [ɔ̃]: lips tightly rounded ("oh"), through the nose.
in [ɛ̃] = lips spread; on [ɔ̃] = lips rounded. Watch your lips in a mirror.
Arabic has no p, so it slips into b. p = b with NO voice: hand on your throat, no buzz for p, buzz for b. Add a small puff of air on p.
